content.value_statement: AI agents fail when prompts are vague, verbose, or overloaded with low-value context. This skill applies Anthropic context engineering principles to help you write clear, structured, high-signal prompts.
actual_capabilities: Provides prompt engineering standards based on Anthropic context engineering principles
Explains how to structure prompts with clear Markdown sections for background, instructions, examples, and constraints
Guides just-in-time context loading and progressive information discovery instead of full data dumps
Offers a create-prompt workflow for building new prompts step by step
Offers an optimize-prompt workflow for improving existing prompts and reducing token usage
Includes a best-practices checklist and a list of anti-patterns to avoid
limitations: Provides guidance and documentation only; it does not automatically rewrite or test prompts
Does not measure token counts or run prompts against a model on its own
Principles are general and may need adjustment for specific models or domains
Effectiveness depends on the user applying the guidance to their own prompts

use_cases.title: Structure a new system prompt
use_cases.description: A developer building an AI agent uses the create-prompt workflow to organize a system prompt into clear background, instruction, example, and constraint sections.

use_cases.title: Reduce token usage in an existing prompt
use_cases.description: A prompt author uses the optimize-prompt workflow to remove redundant text, convert verbose suggestions to direct instructions, and cut token count while keeping clarity.

use_cases.title: Teach prompt engineering standards to a team
use_cases.description: A technical lead shares these standards so the team writes consistent, high-signal prompts and avoids common anti-patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Get started with prompt basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the prompting skill, explain the core principles of context engineering and why concise, high-signal prompts perform better.

prompt_templates.title: Create a structured prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Follow the create-prompt workflow to help me write a system prompt for an agent that summarizes support tickets. Ask me about the goal, audience, and required context first.
prompt_templates.scenario: Building a new prompt from scratch

prompt_templates.title: Optimize an existing prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the optimize-prompt workflow on the prompt below. Remove redundancy, sharpen instructions, add structure, and show me a before and after comparison.
prompt_templates.scenario: Improving a prompt that is too long or vague

prompt_templates.title: Review a prompt against the standards
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my agent prompt against the prompting skill best-practices checklist and anti-patterns. List each item that passes or fails and give specific fixes for the failures.

output_examples.input: Explain the core principles of context engineering.
output_examples.output: The skill returns three core principles: context is a finite resource, so every token should earn its place; optimize the signal-to-noise ratio by preferring direct language and removing redundancy; and use progressive discovery to load detailed information only when it is needed.

output_examples.input: Optimize this verbose instruction: You should always make sure to validate the user's input before you process it.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests a direct rewrite such as: Validate user input before processing. It explains that the imperative form removes filler words, reduces token count, and states the requirement more clearly.

best_practices: Structure prompts with clear Markdown sections so the model can locate background, instructions, examples, and constraints quickly
Prefer direct, imperative language and remove redundant or overlapping information to raise the signal-to-noise ratio
Load detailed context just in time using references instead of pasting full data dumps into every prompt
anti_patterns: Writing verbose explanations that pad the prompt with low-value tokens
Dumping historical context or entire data sets that the model does not need
Using vague, hedging language such as might, could, or should consider instead of clear instructions

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It provides standards and workflows for writing clear, structured, high-signal prompts for AI agents, based on Anthropic context engineering principles.

faq.question: Does it write or run prompts for me?
faq.answer: It guides you through creating and improving prompts. It does not run prompts against a model or measure token counts on its own.

faq.question: Which AI tools does it support?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Claude Code, and Codex.

faq.question: Do I need coding experience to use it?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation and guidance. Anyone writing prompts for AI agents can use it.

faq.question: What is context engineering?
faq.answer: Context engineering is the practice of curating the smallest set of high-value tokens that maximize the chance of the desired output during model inference.

faq.question: How do the two workflows differ?
faq.answer: The create-prompt workflow helps you build a new prompt from scratch. The optimize-prompt workflow helps you improve an existing prompt by cutting redundancy and adding structure.
